# Minimal encounter model (generated by `design/model.py`)

M_A = 4.5, beta_e = beta_i = 1.0: perpendicular MHD compression r = B2/B1 = 2.780; loss cone sin^2(alpha) < 1/r = 0.360. Assumptions and neglected effects: module docstring.

Energies are those of electrons transmitted downstream, in the downstream plasma frame, in units of the upstream T_e (fraction of all incoming electrons above the threshold). 'null': one encounter, reflected electrons lost upstream (the local-θ_Bn null). 'multi': encounters repeat at the next intersection while the electron reflects (periodic slab).

Reading:
- 'null' loses its reflected electrons upstream; 'multi' brings them back with a larger v_par. Compare the
  columns above 10 and 30 T_e: there the excess is a gain in energy, not only a gain in number.
- The model assumes the return; it has no Ξ in it. In a periodic slab the return is certain once the
  upstream arc lies outside the shock layer (Ξ ≳ 1, not modelled). Above that the excess should not
  depend on L_y.
  It depends on δB_x/B0 (local θ) and on m_i/m_e.
- Without scattering the chain stops after a few encounters: each return raises v_par while v_perp is
  fixed, so the electron falls into the loss cone. A power-law tail needs pitch-angle scattering.
